title: Galactic Games
build: Two G64 disk sides of the original Activision release: a boot program at $00AE that unpacks a resident loader to $B800-$FFFF from tracks 19 to 22, the menu HARRY at $0900, five event files PROG0 to PROG4 (two on side 1, three on side 2) loaded over $0900-$B73F, and a records file RECO

records.c: The five events' entry addresses, which load_event jumps to once the event's file is in: 100m Slither $0B00, Space Hockey $0B01, Psychic Judo $1C14, Head Throwing $1000, Metamorph Marathon $1F9F.
Its high bytes interleaved: Slither's.
event_sides is read from here, as $0909 + the event's number (1 to 5).
The disk side each event's file is on, read as $0909 + the event's number: 0 for the first side (Slither, Hockey), 1 for the second (Judo, Head Throwing, Marathon).
The file name "0:PROG0", its digit set to the event's number less 1.
The name's digit.

Loads event $04 and runs it: unhooks the menu's interrupt ($1082), takes the entry address from $0900 into the JMP at $0970, puts the digit into the name, switches to the ROM character set, prints "EVENT LOADING / PLEASE WAIT", and loads the file from drive 8 through the resident loader at $0800.
After the load: status $40 (the end of the file reached) runs the event through the JMP; anything else prints the disk message and waits for a key.
The JMP to the event's entry, its operand set by load_event.
The JMP's operand, low byte.
The JMP's operand, high byte.

Prints "PLEASE ENSURE THAT THE GALACTIC GAMES DISK" and the side it should be ($09FB label side up, $0A1F label side down, by $08FF), then "PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE"; waits for a key to be let go and pressed, clears the screen and loads again.
The disk message's three parts, each ended by $FF: the first line, "IS LABEL SIDE UP IN THE DRIVE." ($09FB) and "IS LABEL SIDE DOWN IN THE DRIVE." ($0A1F).
"DISK IS LABEL SIDE UP IN THE DRIVE.", ended by $FF.
"DISK IS LABEL SIDE DOWN IN THE DRIVE.", ended by $FF.
"PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE", ended by $FF.
The loading screen: clear screen, light blue, "EVENT LOADING" and "PLEASE WAIT", ended by $FF.
Left over and called by nothing: the end of a serial-bus routine and two banking routines from a build of the loader, up to $0AEF.
Left over: sixteen bytes after it.
The commentator's ball: fourteen sprite shapes, $2C to $39, 64 bytes each.

Ball shape $2E.

Part of ball shape $2F.

The first entry, after the intro: banks the ROMs out ($2550), clears the championship flag ($B800), the last event ($FF), the disk side ($08FF) and the records-changed flag ($08FE), then goes on as menu_return.

The entry from an event's quit: sets up three voices that sound only while the volume is up, which is how the typing clicks, the colours and the character set at $2800 ($D018 = $1A), prints message 0, hooks the interrupt ($1064), and has the commentator say the line for the event just played (message $FF + 1: 1 the welcome after the intro, 2 to 6 after each event). FIRE skips to $0F18.
In the championship ($B800 set), the next event loads by itself, or after the marathon the championship ends; otherwise the records are saved if they changed ($0F41) and the menu runs ($0FF4).

Saves the records: asks for the first side when the second is in (messages 15, 16 and 20, waiting for FIRE), shows "SAVING RECORDS TO DISK", deletes the file RECO ("S:RECO" on the command channel), and saves $BC64-$BC95 as RECO; on a disk error says "ERROR WHILE SAVING RECORDS" and tries again.
"S:RECO", the command that deletes the records file; its last four bytes ($0FE8) are the file name RECO.
Saved: the ball hooked again and the disk marked as the first side ($08FF = 0).
Runs the menu ($2385); choice 6 is the championship, which starts with event 1 and $B800 set; any other loads that event.

Starts event $04: FIRE skips to load_event; if the event's file is on the other side, asks for that side (message 15, then 16 or 17); then waits three seconds, has the commentator describe the event (message $04 + 9) and loads it.
The text cursor's column, which the ball follows.
The text cursor's row, which the ball follows.
Twelve bytes nothing reads.
Points the KERNAL's interrupt vector at the ball's handler ($1120) and turns on sprites 0 to 4, sprite 4 multicolour and twice the size.
Gives the interrupt vector back ($1243) and turns the sprites off.
Waits for the raster to pass line 256: the bottom of the screen.

Puts the ball's five sprites at the text cursor: pointers from $1116 and colours from $111B; X from the cursor's column, Y from its row, and $14 higher while the click sounds, so the ball hops at each letter.
The ball's five sprite pointers; the third ($1118) is the spinning frame.
The third sprite's pointer: the spinning shape.
The ball's five sprite colours.

The ball's interrupt, every frame before the KERNAL's own: steps the ball's spin through the list at $11E0; every three frames clicks (volume up) when the cursor has moved a column or a row, and moves the ball to it ($10AB); every two frames steps sprite multicolour 2 through the list at $11D7.
The click's frame count ($11D4, 3), the colour's frame count ($11D5, 2) and place in its list ($11D6).
The colour's frame count.
The place in the colour list.
The colours the ball flashes through, ended by $FF.
A byte nothing reads.
The cursor's column ($11DD) and row ($11DE) at the last click.
The row at the last click.
The place in the spin list.
The ball's spin: pairs of a sprite shape and the frames it shows, ended by $FF.
ball_irq's work: the cursor's line address less $0400, counted down by 40 to its row.
Its high byte.
The KERNAL's interrupt vector, saved by menu_return.
The saved vector's high byte.
The frames left of the spin's current shape.

The commentator says message A: banks the ROMs in, then types the message a character at a time through CHROUT, with a pause after each ($13C3): two frames for a letter, three for a space, twenty for "$"; $0C clears the text ($1333) and $0D starts a new line ($12FE). FIRE on any device can skip the rest ($12DB).

FIRE while the commentator speaks: ignored while $07 is set (from the end of the comment after an event); otherwise silences the click, prints message 0, and jumps through ($08), throwing away the stack.
A new line: slides the ball back to column 2, then moves the cursor down a row, scrolling the text up ($1378) when it is on the last row ($13C2).
Clears the text: rows 1 to 18 blanked and the ball slid back to column 2, row 2.
Scrolls rows 2 to 18 of the screen and of colour RAM up one row.
A byte between scroll_text and last_row, read by nothing.
The commentator's last row, 18.
Waits X frames, one fewer when bit 7 of $13D0 is set.
pause's flag: counted down when the menu runs and up when an event starts.
The addresses of the commentator's 21 messages, numbered from 0.
The message addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Message 0, nothing: clear screen and light blue, used to blank the text, ended by $FF.
Message 1, the welcome: "WELCOME GALACTI-SPORT FANS TO THE MEGA EVENT OF THE CENTURY......", ended by $FF.
Message 2, after 100m Slither: "OKAY, THAT WAS THE 100M SLITHER OR 'SLITH' AS WE PROFESSIONALS CALL...", ended by $FF.
Message 3, after Space Hockey: "HEY! THAT PUCK IS NICE CHAP REALLY! YOU DIDN'T HAVE TO BASH THE...", ended by $FF.
Message 4, after Psychic Judo: "QUITE A PSYCHIC EXPERIENCE, HUH? WELL, WHEN YOU'VE RECOVERED HOW...", ended by $FF.
Message 5, after Head Throwing: "WELL, YOU OBVIOUSLY DIDN'T LOSE YOUR HEAD OVER THAT ONE! NOW TRY...", ended by $FF.
Message 6, after Metamorph Marathon: "THAT REALLY WAS A GOOD EFFORT. BUT IT'S VERY DIFFICULT TO CRACK THE...", ended by $FF.
Message 7, the menu: "SPACE HOCKEY PSYCHIC JUDO HEAD THROWING METAMORPH MARATHON GALACTIC...", ended by $FF.
Message 8, empty, ended by $FF.
Message 9, empty, ended by $FF.
Message 10, 100m Slither described: "HOLD TIGHT AS WE DESCEND INTO THE MAIN STADIUM FOR THE 100M SLITHER....", ended by $FF.
Message 11, Space Hockey described: "NOT AN OPTICAL ILLUSION! HERE IS YOUR CHANCE TO BE AN EYE WITNESS TO...", ended by $FF.
Message 12, Psychic Judo described: "MIND GAMES FOR THOSE WITH A STRONG STOMACH! KNOWN AS THE BELCHING...", ended by $FF.
Message 13, Head Throwing described: "THOSE HUNKY HURLING HRUNTANS FROM THE PLANET JAVELOS ARE STICKING...", ended by $FF.
Message 13 goes on.
Message 14, Metamorph Marathon described: "IS IT A RIGHT-BREASTED, LESSER SPOTTED GORABIRD FROM CLUTOCUS? IS IT...", ended by $FF.
Part of message 14, the marathon described.
Message 15, the disk prompt: "PLEASE ENSURE THAT THE GALACTIC GAMES", ended by $FF.
Message 16, label side up: "DISK IS LABEL SIDE UP IN THE DRIVE", ended by $FF.
Message 17, label side down: "DISK IS LABEL SIDE DOWN IN THE DRIVE", ended by $FF.
Message 18, the save error: "ERROR WHILE SAVING RECORDS", ended by $FF.
Message 19, saving records: "SAVING RECORDS TO DISK", ended by $FF.
Message 20, press fire: "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE", ended by $FF.

The menu: prints it (message 7), unhooks the ball, lights choice 1, and waits: UP and DOWN move the choice (1 to 6, wrapping), its line cycling through the colours at $2477; FIRE takes it. Returns the choice in A, the ball hooked again.
Cycles the chosen line's colours a step, every few frames, and reads the controls ($2422) between steps.
The STY operand: the end of the line's colours, $1D, then moved on.
The LDX operand: the colour list's start, moved on a step each time.
A new choice: the old line back to light blue, waits until the stick is let go on all three devices, and points $02/$03 at the new line's colour RAM ($24D7).

Reads the three devices ($24E5): FIRE returns carry set with A = the current choice (1 to 6); UP or DOWN moves the choice and returns carry set with A = 0; nothing, or only LEFT or RIGHT, returns carry clear.
Joystick two.
The colours the chosen line cycles through: 1 to 10, 13 and 14, repeated.
The colour RAM addresses of the menu's lines, by choice.
The colour rows' high bytes, interleaved.
Reads device A as a joystick, a 1 bit for each held: 0 the keyboard (@ up, : down, H left, K right, the up-arrow key fire), 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.
read_device's work byte.

Banks the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out (and the I/O), keeping A.
